subject: Day 7: weight check this week; SSN and insurance deadline
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 7. Weight-regain window opens this week. Most term infants are back to birth weight by day 14, with the steepest catch-up between days 7 and 10. Operations rhythm now: feed, diaper, 60-90 minutes of sleep, repeat, around the clock.

Action items
- Confirm the first-week pediatrician visit is on the calendar for this week (target day 7-10). The pediatrician wants to verify Avi's weight-regain trajectory. AAP Bright Futures periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Apply for the Social Security Number if the hospital did not file form SS-5. SSA application: https://www.ssa.gov/ssnumber/. The card typically arrives 2-4 weeks after application; you need it to open the 529 plan and claim Avi as a dependent.
- Add Avi to your health insurance plan within 30 days of birth as a qualifying life event. This is a hard deadline. Healthcare.gov reference on QLEs: https://www.healthcare.gov/glossary/qualifying-life-event/
- Order another 4-6 weeks of postpartum pads, two backup tubes of nipple cream (lanolin or Silverette), and 50 more burp cloths. The registry quantity is always short.
- Establish a night-shift split if both parents are home. The 11pm-3am / 3am-7am rotation is more sustainable than both parents up for everything. ACOG postpartum care overview: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management
- Start a feeding log (notes app or Huckleberry): feed start time, side or volume, duration, output. The pediatrician will ask at the 1-month visit.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cord stump drying and detaching between days 5-15. A small spot of blood when it falls off is normal.
- [low concern] Baby acne (neonatal cephalic pustulosis) appearing around week 3-4; resolves without treatment.
- [monitor] Yellow tinge persisting beyond day 14 despite phototherapy. Most physiologic jaundice resolves by week 2; persistence warrants pediatric evaluation. AAP HealthyChildren on jaundice: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Jaundice.aspx
- [call within 24h] Redness greater than 1 cm around the umbilical stump or foul odor (omphalitis is rare but emergent). Forceful projectile vomiting after most feeds with weight stagnation may indicate pyloric stenosis (presents weeks 3-6).
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F. Lethargy, persistent inability to wake for feeds, dusky color around the lips. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunity
Narrate one ordinary task in detail during his next awake-alert window: warming a bottle, folding laundry, making coffee. The content does not matter. Conversational turns (not raw word count) predict later language outcomes; Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018 on PubMed: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/. Two minutes counts.

Upcoming
- Day 7-10: first-week pediatrician visit (target window).
- Day 14-21: first common growth spurt; expect 24-48 hours of feeding-frequency uptick.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens; first social smiles begin.

Further reading
- The Wonder Weeks by Plooij and van de Rijt — developmental leaps framework: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wonder_Weeks
- AAP HealthyChildren on the first month at home: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- ACOG on the postpartum period (week 1-6): https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management
- CDC overview of breastfeeding fundamentals: https://www.cdc.gov/breastfeeding/index.html

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Quiets or turns toward a familiar voice
  AAP window: day 7-45
  What to look for: Voice recognition begins before birth; postnatally it shows as orienting or settling to a parent's voice.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/recognizes-parent-voice/complete

- Watches your face when you talk
  AAP window: day 7-60
  What to look for: Baseline social orientation. Look for sustained gaze, even briefly, during alert windows.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-face-briefly/complete

- Moves both arms and both legs
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-arms-and-legs/complete

- Reacts to loud sounds (startle, blink, stillness)
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Confirms intact hearing response. Universal newborn hearing screen catches most cases but daily observation matters.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/responds-to-loud-sound/complete

- Brings hands within range of eyes and mouth
  AAP window: day 0-45
  What to look for: Early body awareness. Not yet purposeful — looks like accidental discovery.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brings-hands-near-face/complete
